First inspect the supplied project and host contract. Preserve the public importer API, propagate the caller's CancellationToken through operations that can observe it, make disposal deterministic, and avoid sync-over-async. Define the pre-commit and post-commit outcomes before changing code. Verify cancellation at each relevant await boundary, normal completion, parser failure, and that pooled connection counts return to baseline.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the supplied .NET project, host, importer boundary, and relevant environment before acting. Preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=implementation; native C/C++ interop remains a separate near-neighbor) without importing a native boundary that the fixture does not exercise.
Record target frameworks, C# and nullable settings, hosting model, dependency lifetimes, async flow, serializer configuration, and the actual regression command from the supplied project.

Async lifetime and cancellation ownership are explicit: every successfully acquired scope is released exactly once, acquisition failure does not dispose a nonexistent scope, parser or dependency failure leaves the pool at baseline, and cancellation before commit does not publish partial success. Cancellation observed after an irreversible successful commit must not be rewritten as a false rollback.

Run the designated executable regression program or test project, not only dotnet build. Exercise normal completion, parser failure, cancellation before parse, between parse and save, during save, and immediately after commit; record connection-pool baseline and exactly-once disposal. Validate serialization, trimming, or AOT only if the supplied importer contract uses those paths, and label unsupported checks unavailable.

The result must not block async work with .Result or .Wait, capture a scoped importer dependency in a singleton, dispose a resource before ownership is established, or translate a matching OperationCanceledException into an unrelated parser or database failure.
